en.title: Minimum Number of Strictly Decreasing Subsequences
en.description:
Assign every element to exactly one subsequence; each subsequence keeps the original index order and is strictly decreasing. Find the minimum number of subsequences. Subsequences need not be contiguous.

The standard input/output format was compiled by CSWork; value ranges marked "this site" are this site's judging conventions.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n integers; on this site 1≤n≤100000, −10⁹≤a[i]≤10⁹.
en.output: Output the answer required by the problem.
en.explanation: Example 1: it can be split into [5,4,3,1], [2] and [6], and the non-decreasing subsequence [2,4,6] shows at least 3 groups are needed, so the answer is 3. Example 2: the non-decreasing subsequence [2,9,12,13] requires 4 groups, and the greedy approach also splits it into 4 groups. Example 3: equal values cannot go into the same strictly decreasing group, so the answer is 3.
hints: Keep the last values of the decreasing sequences sorted. Append a new value x to the sequence whose last value is the smallest one greater than x; if none exists, start a new sequence. Update using upper_bound binary search.
